canonicalName: Dynamical systems from celestial mechanics (Poincare to Birkhoff)

evidence.claim: Poincare memoir on the three-body problem and equations of dynamics, Acta Math. 13, 1-270
Memoir won King Oscar II prize; first description of chaotic behaviour attributed to it

conceptual.note: Prize awarded 1889; the first printed version contained an error and was withdrawn, the corrected memoir appeared in Acta 13 (1890) (Barrow-Green 1994, cited by MacTutor). Publication year 1890 governs.

evidence.claim: Same 1890 memoir applies geometric (qualitative) methods to the three-body problem
Birkhoff, Proof of Poincare's geometric theorem, Trans. AMS 14 (1913) 14-22

methodological.note: Start = Poincare's own qualitative attack on the three-body problem; end = Birkhoff's 1913 proof of Poincare's last geometric theorem, the first major result by the successor.

evidence.claim: Birkhoff gave the AMS Colloquium lectures of 1920 on Dynamical Systems
Birkhoff, Dynamical systems, AMS Colloquium Publications vol. 9 (1927)

institutional.note: Named lecture series 1920 (history page only); first book titled Dynamical Systems 1927 (bibliographic record; MacTutor gives 1928). Journal Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems came later (1981).

works.citation: H. Poincare, Sur le probleme des trois corps et les equations de la dynamique, Acta Math. 13 (1890) 1-270
works.whyItMatters: Geometric study of orbits in the restricted three-body problem; homoclinic phenomena.

works.citation: H. Poincare, Les methodes nouvelles de la mecanique celeste, Tome I, Gauthier-Villars (1892)
works.whyItMatters: Systematic treatise extending the qualitative methods (periodic and asymptotic solutions).

works.citation: G. D. Birkhoff, Proof of Poincare's geometric theorem, Trans. AMS 14 (1913) 14-22
works.whyItMatters: Settled Poincare's last geometric theorem, continuing his programme.

works.citation: G. D. Birkhoff, Dynamical systems with two degrees of freedom, Trans. AMS 18 (1917)
works.whyItMatters: Early paper using the field name in the modern sense.

works.citation: G. D. Birkhoff, Dynamical Systems, AMS Colloquium Publications 9 (1927)

notes: firstTermUse: earliest JFM/zbMATH title found containing "dynamical system" is Routh 1874 (mechanics sense, not the field); searched ti:"dynamical system(s)" py:1868-1916. Sense of the term as a field name is Birkhoff's (1917/1927). Homoclinic discovery tied to the corrected 1890 memoir (Andersson 1994, Barrow-Green 1994, per MacTutor references).

evidence.claim: Cotes, Logometria, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. (1714)
MacTutor: his work was based on ln(cos q + i sin q) = iq; Logometria his only paper in life

conceptual.note: Attribution of the formula specifically to the 1714 paper (stated geometrically) rests on secondary accounts; the history page ties the formula to his work without explicit year. Harmonia mensurarum (1722) reprints Logometria.

evidence.claim: Harmonia mensurarum (posthumous, ed. R. Smith, 1722)

methodological.note: Uses of the relation for integration appear in the posthumous Harmonia; link of specific integrations to the formula not verified in primary text.

institutional.note: Not meaningful for this event in isolation. Searched for textbook naming: found Euler Introductio in analysin infinitorum (1748, Open Library OL479594W), which gives e^{ix}=cos x+i sin x (MacTutor Euler page) but is not named for the field.
